title: Truncating ASXL1 variants rewire cellular metabolism via mitochondrial pyruvate carrier repression.
abstract: Bohring-Opitz syndrome is caused by heterozygous truncating variants in ASXL1, a chromatin-associated epigenetic regulator forming the PR-DUB complex with BAP1. In patient-derived dermal fibroblasts, truncating variants drove a Warburg-like state with increased glycolytic flux and accumulation of pyruvate and lactate. Truncated ASXL1 and BAP1 showed aberrant co-occupancy at an H3K4me3-marked intronic regulatory element within MPC1 intron 1, with broadened ASXL1 occupancy extending beyond BRD4-defined regulatory boundaries. Pharmacologic MPC inhibition recapitulated both metabolic and Wnt signaling phenotypes.
